# Appeal of Denial – Knee Arthroscopy / Meniscus Surgery (CPT 29881)
### Member: Harper Delgado | Member ID: W267205200 | Reference Number: POC-E2AA78E9EC-43782 | Denial Date: 2026-08-09

**Governing Policy:** Evolent Knee Arthroscopy Prior Authorization Tip Sheet (Evolent_CG-316)
https://www1.radmd.com/sites/default/files/2024-02/2023%20Knee%20Arthroscopy%20Clin%20Tip%20Sheet%20Evolent%2002282024.pdf

Dear Harvard Pilgrim Health Care,

I am writing to appeal the denial of coverage for knee arthroscopy / meniscus surgery (CPT 29881), dated 2026-08-09, reference number POC-E2AA78E9EC-43782. The denial notice states that the documentation submitted was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity. My surgeon, Dr. Reyes, has documented that this surgery is medically necessary, and I am asking the plan to reconsider the request using the complete medical record described below.

## How My Records Address the Plan's Own Criteria

The plan's tip sheet states:

> "The guidelines should be reviewed for additional requirements including duration of symptoms, physical examination, and radiographic criteria and for the complete listing of other procedures not included below."

This tells me that duration of symptoms, physical examination findings, and radiographic criteria are the categories of information the plan uses to evaluate medical necessity. My records address each of these:

**Duration of symptoms and non-operative treatment.** I have had 18 months of progressive knee pain that has not improved with rest. During that time I completed 14 weeks of supervised physical therapy (20 visits, from 2026-03-26 to 2026-07-02) focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note. I also used NSAIDs for 4 months without adequate relief, and received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-13, which gave only 2 weeks of partial relief.

The plan's tip sheet lists qualifying non-operative treatment components, including:

> "oral/topical NSAIDS, acetaminophen, analgesics, tramadol o Brace/orthosis o Physical therapy modalities o Supervised home exercise o Weight optimization o Corticosteroid injection"

and

> "o Rest or activity modifications/limitations o Ice/heat o Protected weight bearing o Pharmacologic treatment:"

My records show supervised physical therapy, pharmacologic treatment (NSAIDs), and a corticosteroid injection — three of the specific treatment types the plan's own list identifies. This treatment also extended well beyond the 12-week duration referenced in the plan's guideline for related knee procedures:

> "Failure of at least 12 weeks of non-operative treatment, including at least two of the following:"

**Physical examination.** My exam findings include positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain. I also experience locking and giving way, and I am unable to squat or kneel and am limited to level walking.

**Radiographic/imaging criteria.** My MRI of 2026-07-14 showed a displaced bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus with mechanical locking, with articular cartilage preserved and a Kellgren-Lawrence grade of 1. The plan's own grading table describes grade 1 as:

> "1 Possible joint space narrowing and osteophyte formation"

This is the mildest category in the plan's own scale, consistent with preserved cartilage and no significant arthritic change — distinct from the more advanced grades the guideline describes. The plan's tip sheet also notes:

> "MRI should not be the primary tool used to determine the presence or severity of arthritic changes in the joint."

I understand this to mean that MRI findings of degenerative change are weighed alongside other findings rather than treated as determinative on their own. I am not aware of a separate radiographic study (such as an x-ray) in my chart, and I am not asserting that one exists; I raise this only because the plan's own note about MRI limitations may be relevant to how the KL grade 1 finding in my MRI report should be interpreted.
